lines: Call for Applications for the 2027–2028 Academic Year
The Digital Humanism Fellowship is part of the

Digital Humanism is an approach that describes, analyzes, and, most importantly, aims to influence the complex interplay between technology and humankind. From 2027 onward, the program will target three major areas of debate surrounding artificial intelligence and its deployment, and therefore invites submissions of research projects that address one of the following thematic areas:

As digital and physical conflicts are increasingly intertwined, and political decisions directly impact the AI sector, particularly regarding energy security and raw material supplies, AI policy necessarily assumes a (geo)political dimension. This focus invites applications that explore this increasingly complex interplay between artificial intelligence, politics, and global cybersecurity.

At the heart of this focus is research that examines the social consequences of the rise of AI, including its implications for the labor market and social inequalities, as well as questions surrounding the acceptance of AI across different areas of society.

AI is fundamentally changing the ways in which culture is created, disseminated, and evaluated. Improved efficiency and economic value, along with the rapid increase in synthetic content, stand in tension with questions of meaning, responsibility, or cultural continuity, calling for profound scientific engagement with the AI-culture interface.
Applications that focus on applying digital means and technologies to research in the humanities cannot be considered.

Fellows will be invited to spend a consecutive three-month term at the IWM between September 2027 and June 2028. Please note that the exact time frame will be determined by mutual agreement and will depend on various factors, in particular the availability of office space.
Fellowships start on the first day of the first month and end on the last day of the last month of the fellowship period.

Postdoctoral candidates who have defended their PhD by the date of the fellowship application deadline will receive a stipend of EUR 3,400 per month; candidates currently pursuing their doctoral degree will receive a stipend of EUR 2,750 per month. From the stipend, visiting fellows are expected to cover all living expenses, including travel to and from Vienna, accommodation costs, health insurance, utilities, local transport, telecommunications, etc., as well as research costs (i.e., for literature or conference fees).

The IWM provides visiting fellows with office space, internet access, in-house research facilities, administrative services, and lunch on workdays, all free of charge. The visiting fellows will join the IWM community of scholars and are invited to participate in the activities of the Institute.

The call for applications is open to academics from all disciplines and regions of the world. Applicants must be enrolled in a doctoral program or have obtained a PhD no more than four years prior to the application deadline (14 January 2023).

We do not accept multiple fellowship applications from the same candidate within the same academic year. Candidates who were previously awarded a fellowship must wait three academic years before applying for another fellowship.
Applications must be submitted through the online application form, which is accessible by clicking on the “Apply” button below. We will not consider applications sent via email.

A concise letter of motivation explaining why a research stay at the IWM and/or in Vienna is relevant to the overall success of the project, how the project relates to the IWM’s mission and research, and what specific goals are to be achieved during the residency
A project description of max. 550 characters incl. spaces
A project proposal of max. 7,500 characters incl. spaces, containing:
a) a description of the project’s objectives, along with an explanation of how it relates to one or more of the three core issues: AI and (geo)politics, AI and society, AI and culture
b) a discussion of the current state of research
A curriculum vitae, including a list of publications

Two letters of recommendation from scholars familiar with the applicant’s academic work. Please note that the letters of recommendation need to be submitted directly by your recommenders before the application deadline. Your recommenders will receive an automatic email with a link to a web form after you have submitted your application.
All application materials must be in English.

Important! Attached documents must be combined into a single PDF, as the online submission form only allows for one attachment. File names of attachments must use Latin characters only. All application materials must be in English.

Applications that meet the specified requirements will be evaluated by a jury of experts. A total of four fellowships will be awarded. The IWM promotes gender equality and aims for a balanced composition of each cohort of fellows. To promote exchange between the Polish and Austrian scientific communities, one fellowship is awarded to a researcher holding Polish citizenship.

Applicants will be notified of the jury’s decision via email by 30 April 2027. Please note that the jury is not required to publicly justify its decisions, nor to provide applicants with individual feedback on their applications.
